figure_inventory.description: A single row of five EMPTY white rectangular boxes (black outline, landscape rectangles, equal size) joined by four plus signs: [ ] + [ ] + [ ] + [ ] + [ ] = 30. The text '= 30' follows the fifth box. No numbers inside any box.

Left to right (counted): purple cards '13' x 3 cards; pink/salmon cards '9' x 4 cards; dark-green cards '1' x 3 cards (top one partly covered); yellow cards '7' x 4 cards; light-green cards '11' x 3 cards; orange/peach cards '5' x 4 cards; light-blue cards '3' x 4 cards. The Kishor question (T6.C35) is judged none/optional, so no item uses it.

Three groups of identical pink (magenta) round dots side by side, each dot set in pairs: (1) a vertical block of 3 rows x 2 columns = 6 dots; (2) a tilted strip of 5 pairs (each pair a short row of 2 dots, rows stepping down to the left from top right to bottom left) = 10 dots; (3) a horizontal block of 2 rows x 9 columns = 18 dots. No leftover single dot in any group (6, 10 and 18 are even). || chunk B note: Teaching picture of even numbers (6, 10, 18) as pairs; no question, solution or worked example of this chunk needs it and no concept image redraws it; the idea is in the topic text.

A single block of round dots, 2 columns x 5 rows = 10 dots, printed to the right of the paragraph. Top 3 rows (6 dots) are green, bottom 2 rows (4 dots) are purple. It shows two even numbers (6 green + 4 purple) joined, still all in pairs. || chunk B note: Teaching picture of a sum of two even numbers (6 + 4) still in pairs; no item needs it and no concept image redraws it.

Three groups of dots side by side, each made of pink pairs plus ONE extra dark navy-blue dot: (1) a vertical block of 3 rows x 2 columns of pink dots (6) with one navy dot below the left column = 7 dots; (2) a tilted strip of 10 pink dots in pairs (5 pairs, stepping down to the right from top left to bottom right) with one navy dot at the bottom end = 11 dots; (3) a horizontal block of 2 rows x 9 pink dots (18) with one navy dot at the right end of the bottom row = 19 dots. The navy dot is the unpaired leftover in each. || chunk B note: Teaching picture of odd numbers (7, 11, 19) as pairs plus one extra dot; closest concept image is the 'extra dot' picture C32.IMG1 (accounting only).

One block of round dots, 2 columns x 6 rows = 12 dots, printed to the right of the paragraph. Green dots: the first 3 rows (6 dots) plus the left dot of row 4 = 7 green. Purple dots: the right dot of row 4 plus rows 5 and 6 (4 dots) = 5 purple. Three blocks of 2-column dot arrays of increasing height, bottoms aligned, left to right (green + purple dots, rows of 2): (1) 3 rows = 6 dots: 3 green (row 1 both, row 2 left) + 3 purple (row 2 right, row 3 both); (2) 4 rows = 8 dots: 5 green (rows 1 and 2 both, row 3 left) + 3 purple (row 3 right, row 4 both); (3) 6 rows = 12 dots: 3 green (row 1 both, row 2 left) + 9 purple (row 2 right, rows 3 to 6 both).
